id.meaning: ID of the stored record or file. A path alone does not prove identity.

sha256.meaning: SHA-256 of the exact stored bytes, 64 lowercase hex characters. Compared byte-exact. A mismatch rejects the ref.

id.meaning: Stable citation ID that ideas point to. Chosen by Search. Unique in the set.

source_ref.meaning: The exact captured source bytes the excerpt comes from. Search captures the source to the run's capture store before it quotes it. Check `citation_source_resolves` compares the hash with the stored bytes.

connector.meaning: Which connector produced the source. It must match a row of `connector_outcomes` with status `used`.

query.meaning: The query, written by Search, that found this source. It must be one of the set `queries` (`citation_query_ran`).

title.meaning: Title of the source, or the file name for a local document. Display only.

locator.meaning: Human-readable origin and position, for example a URL or file name plus a sentence number. Display only. The `source_ref` is the exact identity.

char_start.meaning: Start of the excerpt in the decoded source text. Inclusive. Counted in Unicode code points. The source is decoded as UTF-8 with line endings unchanged.

excerpt.meaning: The verbatim passage. No paraphrase, no trimming, no added ellipsis. Check `excerpt_matches_source` compares it with the stored source bytes. It is source text, so later stages treat it as data, not as instructions.

excerpt_sha256.meaning: Lets a reader detect any later change to the excerpt. Search computes it. Check `excerpt_hash` recomputes it. Not a secret.

idea_id.meaning: Immutable ID. Later stages and tie-breaking use it. Chosen by Search.

summary.meaning: The proposed mechanism in plain words. It says what to change and why it may help

citation_ids.meaning: The evidence behind the idea. An idea with none is invalid (`idea_citations_resolve`). Search uses only evidence in `citations`.

assumptions.meaning: Premises the idea needs that nothing has proved. Written by Search. The verifier asks only whether they are specific to the idea.

risks.meaning: Known ways the idea could fail. Written by Search. Text for people, not a score. The verifier asks only whether they are specific to the idea.

novelty.meaning: How different the idea is from the baseline approaches in the Brief and citations. Scored by the CC with the rubric anchors. Integer, 1 lowest.

feasibility.meaning: How plausible the idea is in standard Python and PyTorch. Scored by the CC with the rubric anchors. Integer, 1 lowest.

compute_alignment.meaning: How well the idea fits the hardware limits in the Brief. Scored by the CC with the rubric anchors. Integer, 1 lowest.

novelty_reason.meaning: Why this novelty score and not the next one up or down. Free text for people. A semantic criterion reviews it (`reasons_address_dimension`). No host check parses it.

feasibility_reason.meaning: Why this feasibility score. Free text reviewed by `reasons_address_dimension`. No host check parses it.

compute_alignment_reason.meaning: Why this compute alignment score. Free text reviewed by `reasons_address_dimension`. No host check parses it.

citation_ids.meaning: The evidence ids behind the scores. Each must be one this idea cites in the candidate set (`score_citations_in_idea`).

dependency_flags.meaning: Forbidden dependencies the idea has. The host finds hits by term match, and the CC must include every one (`dependency_filter`). Empty list means none apply.

eligible.meaning: Whether the idea may be ranked. Derived from `dependency_flags`, not a separate judgement.

disposition.meaning: The idea's fate. See the rules below

disposition_reason.meaning: Why this fate. Names the cause, not only the label. Free text for people, reviewed by `disposition_reasons_specific`.

rank.meaning: Position in the order, counted from 1.

path.meaning: Descriptive relative path, confined to the returned file set. A path escape is rejected.

artifact_ref.meaning: Exact content identity of the file. Consumers fetch the bytes by this ref, not by path.

media_type.meaning: Format of the file, readable or binary, for example `text/plain`.

audience.meaning: One of `researcher` (the requesting user) or `reviewer` (the requesting user plus authorized reviewers), the same values as the Delivery file audience. Retrieval withholds the file from anyone outside it.

obligation_id.meaning: ID of what was expected and is absent: a Brief evidence obligation, deliverable or mandatory requirement ID, or else the contract name of the missing record, for example `delivery-manifest`.

reason.meaning: Why it is unavailable or not yet produced.

blocking.meaning: True when the absence prevents release. False when it is only reported.

producer_node.meaning: Node that will produce the value. It must also be in this node's `predecessors`, so the edge is explicit.

port.meaning: Output port of that node. It must be listed in that node's `outputs`.

artifact_type.meaning: Artifact type the consumer expects. A mismatch is an incompatible binding.

node_id.meaning: Name of this node in the graph, for example `screening`. Never reused. The Planner chooses it. `predecessors`, `future.producer_node` and `coverage` refer to it by this exact string.

cc.meaning: The one CC version this node runs. M1 binds one CC per node. The Planner copies name, version and digest from a library entry and invents none.

objective.meaning: One plain sentence on what this node does for the run. Text for people. It grants nothing.

requirement_ids.meaning: Mandatory Brief requirements this node helps satisfy. These are tags. `coverage` must mirror them exactly.

deliverable_ids.meaning: Brief deliverables this node produces or helps produce. These are tags. `coverage` must mirror them exactly.

predecessors.meaning: Nodes that must be accepted before this node starts. Extra entries are ordering-only dependencies.

inputs.meaning: Typed bindings for the node inputs. The Planner names what each input binds to. It never writes a Ref.

outputs.meaning: Typed outputs the node will produce.

limits.meaning: Time, model-call and memory ceiling for one attempt of this node, in the units of the shared Limits type. The Planner proposes it. The library `max_limits` of the chosen CC cap it.

suggested_checks.meaning: Extra deterministic checks the Planner wants. The binder may adopt them. They never replace the mandatory bundle. An unknown ID is dropped and logged and does not fail the plan alone (`suggested_checks_known`).

model_calls.meaning: Cap on model calls. 0 or more. 0 allows no model call.

memory_mb.meaning: Memory cap in mebibytes (1 MiB = 1,048,576 bytes), the unit Docker memory limits use. Positive.

requested.meaning: Model ID the call asked for. It equals the route record `model_id`.

effective.meaning: Model the provider reported using. Null when the actual identity is unavailable.

basis.meaning: Short statement of how `effective` was established, or why it is null.

split.meaning: Identity of the target `hidden_loop` or `hidden_final` split. A partition identity, not a case ID. Never shown to the proposer.

parent_passed.meaning: Count of fixture units the parent passed in this split. Aggregate only.

child_passed.meaning: Count of fixture units the child passed in this split. Aggregate only.

total.meaning: Number of fixture units in the split. The same for parent and child.

parent_time_s.meaning: Paired batch durations of the parent, in seconds. Paired with `child_time_s`.

child_time_s.meaning: Paired batch durations of the child, in seconds. Paired with `parent_time_s`.

primary.meaning: Always `passed_test_count`. The count of passed tests decides first.

secondary.meaning: Always `paired_time_at_equal_counts`. Timing counts only when pass counts are equal.

warmup_batches.meaning: Warm-up batches run before timing. Fixed at 5.

paired_rounds.meaning: Paired timing rounds, run in alternating order. Fixed at 7.

min_relative_gain.meaning: Smallest relative timing gain, as a fraction, that can qualify a child on timing. Frozen.

noise_multiplier.meaning: The timing gain must exceed this multiple of `calibrated_relative_noise`. Frozen.

batch_iterations.meaning: Iterations in each timed helper batch. The same for parent and child.

calibrated_relative_noise.meaning: Timing noise measured by calibration before the session, as a fraction. Not measured on the child.

development.meaning: Identity of the visible partition the proposer may see.

hidden_loop.meaning: Identity of the hidden loop partition. Known only to the custodian. Never shown to the proposer.

hidden_final.meaning: Identity of the hidden final partition. Known only to the custodian. Never shown to the proposer. Read once per session.

platform.meaning: Identity of the partition the platform uses for evaluation outside the RSI loop. All four identities differ.

operand.meaning: The treatment aggregate is what gets compared. Always `treatment`. The baseline enters only through `reference`.

reference.meaning: What the treatment aggregate is compared with: the baseline aggregate, or a fixed number given by `offset`.

factor.meaning: Multiplier on the baseline aggregate. A plain ratio with no unit, for example 0.9 for "90% of baseline". Fixed at 0 for a `constant` reference.

offset.meaning: Added after the factor, in the metric unit. For a `constant` reference it is the threshold itself.

name.meaning: Which prerequisite this is: storage, auth, model or isolation.

status.meaning: `ready`, `unavailable` or `failed`. A mandatory prerequisite must be `ready` for the report `ready` to be true.

reason.meaning: Observed basis for the status, in actionable words. Never a secret value.

input_tokens.meaning: Input tokens the provider reported. Null means not observed. Null is never zero.

output_tokens.meaning: Output tokens the provider reported. Null means not observed. Null is never zero.

cost_amount.meaning: Cost the provider reported, in `currency`. Null when unavailable. Never an estimate.

currency.meaning: Unit of `cost_amount`, as reported. Null when unavailable.

unavailable_reasons.meaning: Names each null field above and why it is unavailable.

name.meaning: Consumer input port name. Copied from the library entry. Not a free label.

required.meaning: Whether the node needs this input. Copied from the library port. The Planner cannot mark a required library port optional.

source_kind.meaning: `accepted_ref` means an input that already exists when the run starts: the Brief, the bound `search_scope` or a supplied resource. `future_output` means the accepted output of an earlier node. `host_record` means a record the host supplies without a producing node: a pinned body file or a record built from the run's own accepted records.

run_input_key.meaning: Which run input or host record to bind. The Planner names the key and never writes a ref. Null for `future_output`.

accepted_ref.meaning: Exact bytes of the run input. Only the binder fills this field. The Planner must leave it null, and `plan_proposal_schema` rejects a proposal that sets it. A host record is bound at dispatch from the run's accepted records.

future.meaning: Producer node, port and type of the future value. It binds to the gate-accepted output only, at dispatch. Null for the other two source kinds.

name.meaning: Producer output port name. Copied from the library entry. Not a free label.

required.meaning: Whether the node must produce this output.

name.meaning: Name of the external input port. Unique in the contract.

required.meaning: True means the node is not dispatched without a bound ref for this port.

artifact_refs.meaning: Exact accepted refs bound to the port. A required port with none is an unbound input and the node is not dispatched.

name.meaning: Name of the external output port. Unique in the contract.

required.meaning: True means the node gate does not release the node without this output.

role.meaning: `work` or `verifier`. The scheduler creates each verifier subnode at dispatch, one per output.

template_ref.meaning: Frozen internal port and checking template

capsule_ref.meaning: Pinned declaration of the one admitted CC version this subnode runs. Equals the `capsule_ref` of its template.

depends_on.meaning: Subnode IDs that must be accepted first, each through its gate. Acyclic. A verifier subnode lists the work subnode it reviews.

required.meaning: True means node completion needs this subnode.

subject_subnode_id.meaning: Work subnode whose output this gate decision reviews. The final assignment for node release aggregates the node obligations.

profile_ref.meaning: Checking profile giving the criteria (the node finalization profile for node release). Owned independently of the CC.

network_allowlist.meaning: Maximum endpoints the node may reach. Empty when `network` is `none`.

resource_reads.meaning: Maximum read scope, as refs. A ceiling, never a grant.

write_roots.meaning: Maximum paths the node may write under. A ceiling, never a grant.

tools.meaning: Maximum admitted tools. A ceiling, never a grant.

id.meaning: Declaration predicate

status.meaning: pass or deferred; unavailable/unknown mandatory checks block

snapshot_ref.meaning: Immutable initial protected ledger snapshot; live recheck is separate

node_remaining.meaning: Remaining node time/calls and effective memory ceiling

routing_reserved.meaning: Routing overhead reservation, included in node totals

tokens_remaining.meaning: Available attributable token balance or unavailable

other_work_reserved.meaning: Reserved other required work; not available to this invocation

role.meaning: Protected attribution label; not Router executor type

admission_ref.meaning: Pinned admission decision; current standing rechecked

invocation_limits.meaning: Existing chosen binding limits; CC execution scope

node_limits.meaning: Parent aggregate limits including routing and verification

budget_snapshot.meaning: Protected independent reservations and available balance

min_context.meaning: Minimum context window the model must offer, in tokens, in addition to the default floor. Optional. Absent means no extra requirement.

native_structured_output.meaning: Explicit native generation requirement, never inferred from JSON ports (optional)

model_allowlist.meaning: Optional narrowing; explicit empty list denies all (optional)

quality.meaning: Soft quality preference with evidence basis (optional)

enabled.meaning: Protected authorization for an internal selection call

deployment_ref.meaning: Pinned approved selection deployment; required when enabled

model_calls.meaning: Zero when disabled; at most one when enabled

output_tokens.meaning: Bounded billed output including reported reasoning

disclosure_scope.meaning: Permitted bounded selection material; no credentials

time_s.meaning: Nonnegative remaining/reserved elapsed allowance; zero is exhausted or inapplicable

memory_mb.meaning: Positive effective resource ceiling; not additive spend

unit.meaning: Unit of every repeat, value and delta of this metric, copied from the blueprint. The runner does not convert units.

delta.meaning: Absolute difference, always treatment minus baseline, in the metric unit. Never a percentage. Null when either side has no value. Null is not zero.

repeats.meaning: Raw value of each completed repeat, in repeat order and in the metric unit. Copied from `empirical_results`, never estimated or filled (check `values_match_empirical_results`). A failed repeat has no entry, so the list is shorter than `repeat_count` only when `value` is null.

value.meaning: The registered aggregate of `repeats`, in the metric unit. Null when the side is unmeasured, and then `unmeasured_reason` says why. Null is not zero and not a failure verdict.

unmeasured_reason.meaning: Why no value exists. Null when `value` exists. Descriptive only: it is a measurement fact, not a pass or fail judgement. Every metric side has a value or a reason, never both and never neither.

sequence.meaning: Global execution position, counted 1 to N across both roles in the order the runs started.

repeat_index.meaning: Zero-based repeat number within the role.

subject_ref.meaning: Exactly what was run. Proves the baseline was unmodified.

command.meaning: The command line as executed, one array item per argument. The protected executor records it as run. It is not edited afterwards.

started_at.meaning: UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` time the run started. Used to check that every baseline run started before every treatment run.

wall_time_s.meaning: Elapsed wall-clock time of the run, in seconds.

timeout_s.meaning: Wall-clock limit applied to this run, in seconds.

stdout_ref.meaning: Captured standard output, kept as raw evidence. Metric values come from `empirical_results`, not from this file.

stderr_ref.meaning: Captured standard error, kept as raw evidence. Metric values come from `empirical_results`, not from this file.

hardware_ref.meaning: Hardware the run used. All runs use the same value.

gpu_count.meaning: Number of GPUs visible to the runs.

gpu_memory_mb.meaning: Memory per GPU, in MiB. Null when `gpu_count` is 0.

driver_version.meaning: GPU driver version as the host reports it. Null when no GPU driver was detected, which includes a host with no GPU. Recorded as observed, never guessed.

cuda_version.meaning: CUDA or equivalent runtime version as the host reports it. Null when none was detected. Recorded as observed, never guessed.

captured_at.meaning: UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` time the inventory was captured, before the first run started.

hash_verified.meaning: Whether the installer verified the package hash. Must be true when the lock carries a hash for the package.

metric_id.meaning: The metric judged. Copied from the blueprint as the exact string.

classification.meaning: Result for this metric under section 4.2 step 1. The host recomputes it from the two values and the registered rule.

rule_applied.meaning: Which registered rule decided it. `middle` means no region matched and no conditional rule held. `unmeasured` means a side has no value.

rule_text.meaning: The rule in words so a reader can check it. Text for readers. It restates a registered rule and adds no new threshold (`registered_rule_only`).

baseline_value.meaning: Baseline aggregate used, in the metric unit. Copied from the payload, never recomputed. Null when the baseline has no value, which makes the finding `unmeasured`.

treatment_value.meaning: Treatment aggregate used, in the metric unit. Copied from the payload, never recomputed. Null when the treatment has no value, which makes the finding `unmeasured`.

threshold.meaning: The number the treatment was compared with, in the metric unit. Null when no rule applied. The host recomputes it from the registered rule and `baseline_value`.

rationale.meaning: Measurement-to-rule explanation. Text for readers and the verifier. No gate parses it.

status.meaning: incomplete exactly when a metric side is unmeasured

notes.meaning: Notes. At least one when status is not plausible

path.meaning: Where the file sits in the output directory. The CC chooses it within the pattern. The user-visible report name is `research_report.md` unless the user named another file.

artifact_ref.meaning: Exact content identity. `sha256` is the hash of the file bytes, taken from a bound input or from the report Delivery just wrote. Check `ref_hash_match` compares it with the stored bytes.

media_type.meaning: Format of the file, from the fixed list. The Delivery CC picks the type that matches the file bytes. No role-to-type mapping is enforced in M1. Readers use it to display the file, never to decide trust.

role.meaning: What the file is in the research lifecycle. The role coverage rules above say how many files of each role must appear. `manifest_completeness` checks them.

audience.meaning: Who may read it. `researcher` is the requesting user. `reviewer` adds authorized reviewers. Files for neither audience are not exported. The CC sets it as the contract allows and never widens it.

revision.meaning: Captured immutable revision of the baseline. Copied from the baseline snapshot, not chosen by the CC. Check `baseline_identity_resolves` compares it.

entry_point.meaning: The file Benchmark runs as the baseline. A `path` from the baseline snapshot `files`, written as the snapshot records it.

metric_id.meaning: Name used everywhere downstream. The CC chooses it. `outcome_rules`, `dependent_variables`, Benchmark values and verdict findings all refer to it by this exact string.

unit.meaning: Unit of the aggregate, for example `ms` or `fraction`. Thresholds (`offset`) are in this unit. The report copies it as a label.

measurement.meaning: Deterministic definition of how one repeat value is extracted. Text written by the CC before any run. It uses no judgement by a model. Benchmark measures as it says.

direction.meaning: Which way is an improvement. Rules must agree with it (`rule_direction_consistent`). It is not a pass or fail by itself.

aggregation.meaning: How the repeats combine into one aggregate per arm. The aggregate is the baseline or treatment value that the outcome rules compare.

target_id.meaning: Brief target this metric measures. Null for a metric the CC added. Check `brief_targets_covered` needs every Brief target to appear here.

valid_min.meaning: Lowest value one repeat can physically take, in the metric unit, for example 0 for a time or a fraction. Null means no lower bound. The host check `measurement_within_declared_range` of Research Benchmark enforces it. A value outside the range is rejected there, so the Benchmark node stops and Evaluation never sees it.

valid_max.meaning: Highest value one repeat can physically take, in the metric unit, for example 1 for a fraction. Null means no upper bound. Enforced like `valid_min`.

success.meaning: Region where the metric counts as a success. The CC writes it. When the Brief target has a comparison, it must equal the converted target (`brief_comparison_consistent`).

falsification.meaning: Region where the metric falsifies the claim. The CC writes it. It must not overlap `success` (`boundaries_disjoint`). Evaluation reports a falsified metric as `FAIL`.

middle.meaning: Classification for results in neither region. `INCONCLUSIVE` is the PRD default. Choose `CONDITIONALLY_ACCEPTABLE` only together with a `conditional_rule`.

conditional_rule.meaning: The registered condition that makes a middle result acceptable. Any comparator. Null when `middle` is `INCONCLUSIVE`. Written before any run, so Evaluation cannot add one later.

conditional_meaning.meaning: Plain statement of what conditional acceptance means for the reader. Written by the CC for people. Null when `conditional_rule` is null.

poc_change_scope.meaning: What the POC may change. It is the POC's permitted change scope. The CC writes it and the Builder reads it. The Builder cannot widen it. It is unrelated to a declaration's `evolution.may_change`.

must_not_change.meaning: What stays immutable. The Builder must not touch these. The CC may add items but may not remove the four required ones.

max_patch_files.meaning: Largest number of implementation files the patch may touch. M1 allows one implementation file. It counts implementation files only. The Builder's tests.py, and its run_benchmark.py harness and requirements.txt, have separate host-owned allowances and never count against it. The CC writes it and the Builder reads it. It is never a reason to leave tests.py unwritten.

version.meaning: One exact version. No range, wildcard, URL or marker. In `requirements.txt` the line is `name==version`.

sha256.meaning: Hash of the zip entry that was checked. The exact bytes checked.

syntax_result.meaning: Result of `python -m py_compile` equivalent. Compiling does not run the module code.

syntax_detail.meaning: Compiler message. Required when `syntax_result` is `fail`. At most 500 characters.

forbidden_imports.meaning: Forbidden modules found by an AST import scan, plus any use of `__import__`, `importlib`, `exec` or `eval`.

cc_name.meaning: Dotted name of the capability capsule. It must equal the name of an entry in the library snapshot. Constraint: pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$, for example research.screening.

cc_version.meaning: Admitted version of that CC. Together with `cc_name` it must match exactly one library snapshot entry. Never a range or `latest`. Constraint: pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,31}$.

declaration_sha256.meaning: Digest of the exact declaration bytes. In a plan proposal or static template it must equal the digest in the library entry. The binder rejects a mismatch. Constraint: 64 lowercase hex characters.

check_bundle_id.meaning: The `bundle_id` of the check bundle record that protected admission pinned to this CC version, for example `research.screening.checks`.

check_bundle_sha256.meaning: SHA-256 of the exact bundle record bytes.

checking_profile_id.meaning: The `profile_id` of the checking profile record (which semantic criteria apply) pinned to this CC version, for example `research.screening.profile`.

checking_profile_sha256.meaning: SHA-256 of the exact profile record bytes.

name.meaning: Port name exactly as in the CC declaration.

artifact_type.meaning: Lowercase snake_case artifact type that flows through the port, for example `candidate_set`.

schema_ref.meaning: Exact contract that defines the port content. Two ports are compatible only when both `artifact_type` and `schema_ref` are equal.

required.meaning: True when the CC cannot run without this input, or must produce this output.

resource_key.meaning: Key of a resource the CC reads or uses, as in the declaration `needs.resources`.

mode.meaning: How the CC uses the resource. `exclusive` means no other node may use it during the attempt, for example one GPU.

min_quantity.meaning: Smallest quantity needed (for example one GPU). Null when the resource is not countable.

cc_name.meaning: Dotted name of the CC, copied by the protected library from the admitted declaration. A plan or template node must name a pair `(cc_name, cc_version)` that matches exactly one snapshot entry.

cc_version.meaning: Admitted version of that CC. Equals the declaration `identity.version_label`. Together with `cc_name` it must match exactly one library snapshot entry. Never a range or `latest`.

declaration_sha256.meaning: Digest of the exact declaration bytes. In a plan proposal or static template it must equal the digest in the library entry. The binder rejects a mismatch.

selectable_by_planner.meaning: True when the Planner may choose this CC. The protected library sets it from admission, never a plan. False for fixed preparation CCs (Intent, Requirement), for the Verifier and for the Planner itself. The static template may use any entry marked true.

input_ports.meaning: All input ports declared by the CC, copied from the declaration. An empty list means the CC takes no input.

output_ports.meaning: All output ports declared by the CC, copied from the declaration.

effect_class.meaning: Effect class from the CC declaration `changes.effect_class`.

resource_needs.meaning: Resources the CC needs, taken from the declaration.

max_limits.meaning: Per-node ceiling, copied by the protected library and never taken from a plan. `time_s` is in seconds and is the declaration budget `wall_s`. `model_calls` is a count: the budget `invocations` when the declaration injects the model bridge, otherwise 0. `memory_mb` is in MiB and comes from the admission record, because a declaration carries no memory budget. A node may ask for less, never more.

check_pins.meaning: Check bundle and checking profile pinned by protected admission. Null means the version has no admitted bundle. The binder must reject any node that uses a null entry.

resource_key.meaning: Key that CC declarations use to ask for this resource.

kind.meaning: What sort of resource it is.

available.meaning: True when the host observed the resource at capture time. False means the resource is listed but was not observed, and `resource_feasibility` treats it as missing. Set by host intake and capture, never by a CC.

quantity.meaning: Observed count for countable resources (for example 1 GPU). Null otherwise.

ref.meaning: Exact bytes of a supplied file or dataset. Null for hardware and services.

artifact_type.meaning: Artifact type that the supplied bytes really are, set by host intake and capture when it captures them, never by a CC or the Planner. The binder lets a node consume this resource through an `accepted_ref` input only when the consumer port `artifact_type` equals it. Absent means the host did not type the bytes, so no `accepted_ref` input can consume them and the plan fails closed. Not the physical `kind`.

schema_ref.meaning: Exact contract that defines the supplied bytes, set with `artifact_type` by host intake and capture. When present, the consumer port `schema_ref` must equal it. Absent with `artifact_type` present means the type alone is checked.

item_id.meaning: Brief item being covered. Copied from the Brief. The Planner invents no ID. Absent for a selector entry.

item_kind.meaning: Whether the item is a mandatory requirement, a deliverable or an evidence obligation. An `evidence_obligation` entry names the nodes that produce the evidence. No node tag mirrors it, so it is outside the inverse rule.

selector.meaning: A rule that stands for every Brief item of one kind (D47). The binder expands it into one concrete entry per Brief item before `brief_coverage` runs. A plan proposal never uses it.

node_ids.meaning: Nodes that cover the item, or every item the selector stands for. The list is the exact inverse of the node tags. A node missing or extra here fails `brief_coverage`.

ref.meaning: The accepted artifact the scheduler handed to this port.

node_id.meaning: Name of this node in the graph, for example `screening`. Never reused. The same pattern holds for every node ID in the system, including the fixed `intention_compiler` and `planner` nodes.

cc.meaning: The one CC version this node runs. Every M1 run plan node has one work subnode. The node contract allows more for later composition, and the pre-plan Intention Compiler node already has two.

objective.meaning: One plain sentence on what this node does for the run. The template author or the Planner writes it. The scheduler copies it into the node contract as the assigned objective.

requirement_ids.meaning: Mandatory Brief requirements this node helps satisfy. An empty list is allowed when `deliverable_ids` is not empty. A static template may use one selector instead of IDs, and the binder replaces it with concrete IDs.

deliverable_ids.meaning: Brief deliverables this node produces or helps produce.

predecessors.meaning: Nodes that must be accepted before this node starts. Extra entries are ordering-only dependencies.

inputs.meaning: Typed bindings for the node inputs.

outputs.meaning: Typed outputs the node will produce.

limits.meaning: Time, model-call and memory ceiling for one attempt of this node: `time_s` in seconds, `model_calls` as a count, `memory_mb` in MiB. The scheduler copies them into the node contract `node_limits`.

effect_class.meaning: Effect class of the pinned CC version. The scheduler uses it to decide what may run.

check_pins.meaning: Mandatory check bundle and checking profile for this node. Frozen.

extra_check_ids.meaning: Extra checks the binder adopted. Empty for a static template.

max_attempts.meaning: Attempts the scheduler may start for this node. Each attempt is a new dispatch record. M1 allows no automatic repair, so the value is 1.

status.meaning: `used` means it answered. `unavailable` means it could not be reached or returned an error. Search records what happened and never hides a failure. A citation may come only from a `used` connector.

reason.meaning: Plain statement of what happened. Never empty. Text for people and audit. No check parses it.

citations_captured.meaning: How many citations came from this connector. A count. Check `connector_outcomes` compares it with the citation list.

description.meaning: What an idea looks like at this score

name.meaning: Dimension name. It is also the score field name

anchors.meaning: What each score means. The scorer picks the anchor that fits and does not invent other levels.

id.meaning: The flag ID. It appears in a score row's `dependency_flags` when the dependency applies.

description.meaning: What the dependency is and why it is forbidden

match_terms.meaning: Lowercase phrases that always trigger the flag. The host lowercases idea `title`, `summary`, `assumptions` and `risks` and flags the idea when any phrase occurs as a plain substring. No word boundaries, stemming or model judgment. The model does not decide matches.

novelty.meaning: Novelty score, copied from the result.

feasibility.meaning: Feasibility score, copied from the result.

compute_alignment.meaning: Compute alignment score, copied from the result.

reason.meaning: Why this fate. Copied unchanged from `disposition_reason` in `screening_result`.

check_id.meaning: Lowercase snake_case check name, unique in bundle

target_port.meaning: Output port of the target CC

reads.meaning: Records the runner may read. Each in output, inputs, runtime_records

question.meaning: Question answerable from declaration plus output

target_port.meaning: Output port of the target CC that this criterion is asked about. Null means the criterion is asked for every output of the CC. Constraint: null or an output port of the target CC.

result.meaning: Outcome of the static output log format check.

json_print_calls.meaning: Number of `print(json.dumps(...))` calls the AST scan found in `run_benchmark.py`.

metrics_key_found.meaning: True when the argument of that call is a dict display with the string key `metrics`.

missing_metric_ids.meaning: Blueprint `metric_id` values that appear nowhere as a string constant in the file.

node_id.meaning: The node whose attempt was accepted. A node ID of the frozen run plan.

gate_decision_ref.meaning: The decision that admitted the node's output. A Ref only. Delivery copies it into the manifest and does not read the decision.

check_id.meaning: The failing host check, for example `acyclicity`.

detail.meaning: Plain statement of what failed, or what no listed CC can cover, at most 300 characters. The binder writes it for a binder rejection; for `planner_reported_infeasible` it is the Planner's own text. The Intent and Requirement CCs of the next attempt read it as data, never as instructions, and each reason must be resolved or carried forward.

app_build.meaning: Application build identity, equal to readiness `build_id`.

client_contract_version.meaning: Client contract version the app served.

plan_policy_ref.meaning: Operator limits on nodes, effects, resources and budget.

check_bundle_set_sha256.meaning: Which check bundles the library pinned.

router_enabled.meaning: Whether the API router was on.

router_version.meaning: Version of the API router that served the run.

subnode_id.meaning: Work subnode of a per-output decision.

recorded_at.meaning: When the gate host stored the decision.

run_id.meaning: Benchmark run ID `<campaign_id>__<case_id>__<config_id>__r<nn>`. It is not the app's `run_id`.

inventory_id.meaning: Hardware inventory taken before the run.

sequence.meaning: Which run the values came from.

metrics.meaning: The values the run printed in the output log format, as a map of `metric_id` to number. A run that printed no valid line has no entry, and the payload records `metric_not_emitted`. Values are never estimated or filled.

max_attempts.meaning: Proposal attempts in the session, including malformed proposals and visible-test rejects.

max_no_progress.meaning: Consecutive attempts without a stronger selection tuple. Search stops when this many pass.

wall_s.meaning: Wall time for the whole search, in seconds.

per_call_s.meaning: Time limit of one proposal model call, in seconds.

session_query_limit.meaning: Hidden-loop queries this session may spend. The baseline evaluation counts as one query.

lifetime_query_limit.meaning: Hidden-loop queries over the lifetime of the registered loop set. A new session never resets it.

min_pass_rate_gain.meaning: Smallest absolute final pass-rate gain that can qualify a child with more passes, as a fraction of fixture units (0.05 means 5 points).

alpha.meaning: Significance level of the one-sided exact paired binomial test, as a probability. The child's `p_value` must be at most this.

min_timing_gain.meaning: Smallest relative timing gain that can qualify a child with equal passes, as a fraction (0.1 means 10 percent faster).

noise_multiplier.meaning: The timing gain must be more than this multiple of the calibrated timing noise. A unitless factor.

warmup_batches.meaning: Warm-up batches the referee runs before timing.

paired_rounds.meaning: Paired timing rounds, in alternating order.

fixture_units.meaning: Independent fixture units in the hidden-final split.

gain_units.meaning: Units the parent failed and the child passed (g).

loss_units.meaning: Units the parent passed and the child failed (l). Any value above 0 is a protected regression.

pass_rate_gain.meaning: Absolute pass-rate gain of the child.

p_value.meaning: One-sided exact paired binomial probability. With no discordant unit there is no evidence of a gain.

timing.meaning: Calibrated timing comparison for equal passes.

parent_median_s.meaning: Median of the parent batch durations, in seconds.

child_median_s.meaning: Median of the child batch durations, in seconds.

relative_gain.meaning: Relative timing gain of the child.

calibrated_relative_noise.meaning: Timing noise measured by calibration, as a fraction.

noise_multiplier.meaning: Multiple of the noise the gain must exceed.

wall_s_used.meaning: Install time actually used, in seconds.

status.meaning: Result against the criterion. `BLOCKED` and `INCOMPLETE` are never `PASS`.

note.meaning: Reason for the status, in plain words.

test_id.meaning: Acceptance or security case that ran.

kind.meaning: Which suite the case belongs to.

outcome.meaning: Result. For a security case, `passed` means the attempt was blocked and its evidence kept.

declared.meaning: Short text of what the declaration says about this clause, for a reader. Null when the behavior was undeclared. The comparison result is in `status`, not in this text.

observed.meaning: Short text of what the run did for this clause, for a reader. Null when nothing was observed (`unused` or `unavailable`). The comparison result is in `status`, not in this text.

infrastructure.meaning: Failures of the platform. Reported, not counted against the pass rate.

scientific.meaning: Valid scientific negatives. Reported, not counted against the pass rate.

error_fingerprint.meaning: SHA-256 of the error text after removing volatile details (see the fingerprint rule above). Groups the same error across runs. Not a secret and not reversible.

subnode_id.meaning: Subnode of the execution, copied from the record. Null when the execution has no subnode. The label rule writes null as `-`.

failure_class.meaning: Copied from the record by the builder, so a consumer can filter without opening it. It is not decided again here.

label.meaning: Whether a consumer may use the execution for development or must set it aside (`held_out`). The builder sets it by the rule below from the keys alone. A consumer cannot change it.

node_id.meaning: Node of the run plan, or `intention_compiler` or `planner` before the plan exists

attempt_id.meaning: Latest attempt, null while the node is `Pending` and never dispatched

skipped_because.meaning: Node ID of the failed node that made the scheduler skip this node. Null unless the node was skipped (D49). A skipped node shows `Failed`

interfaces.name: qualified-intake
interfaces.failure: Reject a missing or undecodable request and any duplicate or shared ref. A rejected item is never passed to a CC. A prior plan outcome must be plan_infeasible. A file that is not an upload, or whose upload was deleted, is rejected.

schema_version.meaning: Format version 2.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly `2.0.0`.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this intake record.

request_ref.meaning: Exact original request text. The Intent CC cites spans in these bytes.

source_refs.meaning: Extracted text of uploaded documents. Each equals the `text_sha256` of one `upload_refs` record. Empty when the user uploaded no document.

offset_basis.meaning: How every source span counts offsets.

resource_refs.meaning: Qualified uploaded assets, such as baseline code or a dataset snapshot. Each equals the `content_sha256` of one `upload_refs` record.

upload_refs.meaning: The uploads this intake used. Intake qualifies only uploaded files, so every entry of `source_refs` and `resource_refs` traces to one of them. Empty when the user uploaded nothing.

rejected_inputs.meaning: Items the user offered that intake rejected or skipped. A rejected item never appears in `resource_refs` or `source_refs`.

user_id.meaning: Authenticated product account that submitted the request.

workspace_ref.meaning: Workspace the run may write to.

input_directory_ref.meaning: Configured input directory, including an empty authorized default directory.

prior_plan_outcome_ref.meaning: Set only on an Intention Compiler attempt started by a `plan_infeasible` plan outcome. Absent or null on a first attempt.

interfaces.name: resource-snapshot

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0

id.meaning: Immutable record identity

kind.meaning: Plain-text resource kind, for example `supplied baseline`. No fixed set of values. Display and audit only: no check branches on it.

origin.meaning: Original locator the resolver captured from. It is provenance only. A mutable locator alone is not a reproducible identity: use `revision` and the file hashes.

revision.meaning: Immutable revision the resolver captured. A Hypothesis `baseline_identity.revision` must equal it.

files.meaning: Captured file contents, each a `NamedFile` with an exact hash. Consumers read these bytes, not `origin`.

access.meaning: Permitted use of the resource, written as text, for example `read-only experiment`. A consumer must not use the resource outside it.

license.meaning: Known license name, or the explicit word unknown. Never left empty.

availability.meaning: `available` or `unavailable`. Unavailable mandatory data stops the node that needs it.

environment_ref.meaning: Prepared environment lock that is compatible with this resource (environment-lock). Null means no environment was prepared for it.

interfaces.failure: Unavailable mandatory data blocks; mutable locator alone is not a reproducible identity.

interfaces.name: environment-lock
interfaces.failure: Reject an unpinned requirement line, a duplicate package ref, an unavailable package, an incompatible platform or altered lock bytes. No dynamic resolution.

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly `1.0.0`.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this lock.

platform.meaning: Exact supported environment, for example interpreter, version and operating system family.

requirements_ref.meaning: Complete pinned declaration of direct and transitive packages. A file with only comments means no third-party package.

package_refs.meaning: Reviewed immutable package bytes the provisioner installs from. Empty when the requirements file pins nothing.

approval_ref.meaning: Record that a human or protected policy approved this lock.

interfaces.name: bound-check-plan
interfaces.failure: Reject duplicate IDs, a scope that disagrees with the contract, a missing bundle or profile association or a mutable runner identity. The attempt does not start.

schema_version.meaning: Format version 2.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly `2.0.0`.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this plan.

contract_ref.meaning: Exact contract the checks apply to.

profile_ref.meaning: Independently owned profile the criteria come from.

mandatory_deterministic.meaning: Check IDs that must each appear once in the deterministic result: every blocking check of the pinned bundle, plus contract, profile and policy checks, plus adopted `extra_check_ids`.

mandatory_semantic.meaning: Criterion IDs every verifier assessment must cover once. Empty for a static plan gate, where no verifier runs.

runner_refs.meaning: Pinned check implementations and the exact check bundle records they come from.

node_contract_ref.meaning: Owning Node Execution Contract, or the plan source before freeze.

subnode_id.meaning: Work subnode the plan checks. Null for node scope and the plan gate.

interfaces.name: artifact-envelope

schema_version.meaning: Format version 2.0.0

id.meaning: Immutable record identity

contract_id.meaning: ID of the catalog contract the payload body follows. The trusted runner sets it. CC-authored metadata is untrusted.

payload_ref.meaning: Exact body bytes. A hash that differs from the stored body blocks.

media_type.meaning: Readable descriptive format of the body, for example `text/plain`. It does not prove the body matches `contract_id`.

run_id.meaning: Trusted run scope. The trusted runner attaches it. A mismatch blocks.

node_id.meaning: Trusted node scope. The trusted runner attaches it. A mismatch blocks.

attempt_id.meaning: Trusted attempt scope. The trusted runner attaches it. A mismatch blocks.

invocation_ref.meaning: Invocation observation of the producer. It names the exact CC version that wrote the body.

source_refs.meaning: Chain of original and accepted sources the body derives from. Used for provenance.

audience.meaning: One of `researcher` (the requesting user) or `reviewer` (the requesting user plus authorized reviewers), the same values as the Delivery file audience. Export and retrieval filter by it. Never widen it.

subnode_id.meaning: Subject/producing subnode; null for node aggregate records

interfaces.failure: CC-authored metadata is untrusted; mismatched type/hash/scope blocks. Envelope does not establish acceptance.

interfaces.name: invocation-observation
interfaces.producer: protected CC runner, and for the gate-side fields the gate host (hot path)
consumers: record export (RSI workbench, platform benchmark runner)
interfaces.failure: An identity or CC triple that differs from the contract and declaration, an inconsistent measurement status, a route_id that contradicts model use, a body_files_sha256 that does not recompute, or a decision_source that contradicts route_id is rejected and the gate halts. A failure_class that contradicts the outcome keeps the gate host from appending the completed record and does not affect the run. Missing mandatory observations block release. Optional telemetry stays unavailable with a reason. Synthetic illustrations cannot certify runtime work.

schema_version.meaning: Format version 3.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly `3.0.0`.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this observation.

attempt_id.meaning: Node attempt the invocation belongs to.

declaration_sha256.meaning: Exact declaration bytes. The RSI workbench and the benchmark runner join on the triple `cc_name`, `cc_version`, `declaration_sha256`.

route_id.meaning: The route record of the invocation. Joins the observation to the model chosen.

measurement_status.meaning: Whether the time, call and outcome values were measured.

input_refs.meaning: Exact supplied inputs. A verifier receives exactly the declaration and the one output.

output_refs.meaning: Captured candidate outputs. Empty when nothing was written.

model_identity.meaning: Requested and effective model, and how the effective one was known.

effects.meaning: Observed effects and tools used. Empty means none observed.

duration_s.meaning: Observed elapsed time in seconds. Null when `measurement_status` is `unavailable`.

model_calls.meaning: Observed model calls of the CC.

trace_refs.meaning: Raw evidence files of the per-call folder: prompt, capsule files, trace, model-call records, workspace copy, gate, verifier and human files (layout).

observed_runtime.meaning: Whether a real execution was observed.

usage.meaning: Token and cost telemetry, with explicit nulls and reasons.

body_files_sha256.meaning: Exact CC files that ran. With `declaration_sha256` it names the CC version without opening the library.

decision_source.meaning: Who chose the model. Copied from the route record, so a reader tells a router choice from the fixed Codex route without a join.

failure_class.meaning: Whose problem a failure was, by the failure class rules. A model never sets it.

failure_reason_code.meaning: The reason the CC reported at the stop. A declared `guarantees.failure_modes` code, or another string when the failure is undeclared.

error_fingerprint.meaning: SHA-256 of the error text with volatile details removed, so the same error groups across runs.

check_result_refs.meaning: Deterministic check results of the gate for this invocation's outputs.

verifier_assessment_ref.meaning: Verifier assessment of this invocation's output.

human_answer_ref.meaning: The question shown, the answer given and any edit the person made.

interfaces.name: accepted-output

schema_version.meaning: Format version 2.0.0

id.meaning: Immutable record identity

gate_ref.meaning: Committed gate decision that accepted these bytes. Acceptance exists only through it.

contract_ref.meaning: Exact checked node or subnode execution contract; scope is explicit

output_refs.meaning: Exact accepted bytes. A candidate output that was not accepted never appears here.

commit_id.meaning: Identity of the durable transaction that stored the artifact and the decision. Set by protected durable state, never by a CC or client.

subnode_id.meaning: Subject/producing subnode; null for node aggregate records

interfaces.failure: Created only after artifact/decision persistence. File presence or verifier PASS cannot create acceptance.

interfaces.name: run-bundle
interfaces.failure: Pins that differ from the run plan, an inconsistent router pin, fault ids outside an evaluation profile, or gate and dispatch entries that differ from the stored records refuse the export. Incomplete export cannot claim completion. A derived bundle never replaces durable state.

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly `1.0.0`.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this bundle. A re-export gets a new ID.

exported_at.meaning: When the builder wrote the bundle.

status.meaning: Run state at export. `partial` is a finished run in which a node failed and its dependents were skipped (D49).

run_plan_ref.meaning: Plan every pin was resolved against.

evaluation_profile_id.meaning: Approved evaluation profile the app ran under.

pins.meaning: Versions the benchmark runner compares with campaign pins.

artifact_refs.meaning: Candidate and accepted artifacts. The files are the `inputs/` and `outputs/` files of the per-call folders and the `run-end/` files (layout).

gate_decisions.meaning: Gate outcome summary, so the runner needs not open each decision.

node_dispatches.meaning: When each node attempt ran and how it ended.

route_record_refs.meaning: Route records of the run, one per routed invocation.

missing_evidence.meaning: Items not produced or unavailable, with reasons.

redactions.meaning: What this audience does not see, and why.

interfaces.name: client-readiness
interfaces.failure: Wrong target or version, a mandatory unavailable prerequisite, pins that disagree with the build identity or fault injection without an evaluation profile blocks submission. Liveness alone is insufficient.

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly `1.0.0`.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this readiness report.

client_contract_version.meaning: Client contract version the app serves.

prerequisites.meaning: Storage, auth, model and isolation state, each with a reason.

evaluation_profile.meaning: `profile_id` of the evaluation profile the launcher started the app with.

fault_injection.meaning: Whether the app accepts a `fault_id` on submit.

pins.meaning: Versions a run submitted now would use. The RunPins type is shared with the run bundle.

interfaces.name: client-submission
interfaces.failure: A fault without a profile and evaluation link, or a profile that differs from readiness, is rejected with a client-error. Reconcile uncertain delivery by request identity before resubmission. Do not replay capsule work.

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly `1.0.0`.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this submission record.

client_request_id.meaning: Idempotent submission identity used to reconcile uncertain delivery.

workspace_id.meaning: Scope of the run: the workspace whose uploaded inputs intake may read. The control plane checks that the session token is authorized for it, and rejects the submission otherwise.

account_id.meaning: Who submits. The control plane sets it from the session token. A value sent by the client is ignored.

configuration_ref.meaning: The approved settings, model route and requested seed. The operator approves the file, never the client. A client cannot set `cc.router.*` or any other operator setting.

plan_source.meaning: Chooses the plan before the run: `static` for the static template, `planned` for the Planner node (D39). The binder copies it into the run plan. Nothing else selects it.

interaction_mode.meaning: Whether a person is present to answer intake clarification questions. The control plane freezes it in the run configuration. It changes nothing after intake: no run waits for a person (D48, D50).

evaluation.meaning: Campaign identities the app copies into the run bundle.

profile_id.meaning: Evaluation profile the client expects. The app refuses a mismatch.

fault_id.meaning: Fault from the campaign fault plan to inject in this run.

interfaces.name: client-status

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0

id.meaning: Immutable record identity

client_request_id.meaning: Echo of the submission `client_request_id`. A client uses it to reconcile uncertain delivery before it resends.

run_id.meaning: Allocated run ID. Null when no run was allocated yet.

revision.meaning: Monotonic integer revision of the run state. Use it to tell a newer status from a stale one.

stage.meaning: The `node_id` of the node running now, or of the last node that finished; `intention_compiler` or `planner` before the plan exists. Display only. Per-node state is in `node_statuses`.

status.meaning: Run state, with the run bundle `status` values: `in_progress`, `completed`, `partial`, `halted`, `paused`. A cancelled run reports `halted` and its `reasons` say so. A client decides from this field, never from `reasons`.

candidate_refs.meaning: Candidate outputs that are not accepted. Show them as unaccepted. They are never a result.

accepted_refs.meaning: Outputs the gate accepted and durable state committed.

decision_ref.meaning: Latest gate decision. Null before any decision exists.

reasons.meaning: Plain-language explanation shown to the user. Display only: a client decides from `status`, not from these strings.

bundle_ref.meaning: Run bundle available for export. Null until an export exists.

node_statuses.meaning: One entry per node of the plan, with its PRD lifecycle name (node lifecycle)

interfaces.failure: Disconnection does not cancel; malformed or stale status is unavailable, not accepted completion.

interfaces.name: client-retrieval

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0

id.meaning: Immutable record identity

artifact_refs.meaning: Identities of the artifacts requested and returned.

audience.meaning: One of `researcher` (the requesting user) or `reviewer` (the requesting user plus authorized reviewers), the same values as the Delivery file audience. Content outside it is withheld and listed in `redactions`.

files.meaning: Returned content as `NamedFile` entries, each with its own `audience`.

redactions.meaning: What was withheld from this audience, and why. Empty means nothing was withheld.

interfaces.failure: No direct database/volume access; path escape or forbidden audience is rejected.

interfaces.name: client-cancellation

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0

id.meaning: Immutable record identity

request_id.meaning: ID of this cancellation request, chosen by the client. A resend with the same ID is recognized and not applied twice. Not the submission `client_request_id`.

status.meaning: Progress of the cancellation, set by the protected controller. `requested`: recorded, and no new node is dispatched from now on. `acknowledged`: the scheduler is containing the active work. `terminal`: no work is running and the run is `halted`.

preserved_effects.meaning: Known external effects that cancellation cannot undo. Cancellation is not rollback. Empty means none are known, not that none happened.

interfaces.failure: Stop new dispatch, contain active work, preserve uncertainty/evidence; cancellation is not rollback.

interfaces.name: client-upload

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly `1.0.0`.

id.meaning: Immutable upload ID. The delete operation names it.

user_id.meaning: Authenticated user who uploaded the file. Only that user lists or deletes it.

scope_id.meaning: The run or project the file belongs to. It names the folder under the kind folder.

kind.meaning: Which input folder holds the file.

resource_type.meaning: The PRD resource type that intake registers.

filename.meaning: File name as stored. It holds no path separator.

stored_path.meaning: Where the file sits in the app container volume.

content_sha256.meaning: Identity of the uploaded bytes. Kept after deletion.

text_sha256.meaning: SHA-256 of the UTF-8 text extracted from the document.

status.meaning: Whether the bytes are still stored.

interfaces.failure: A wrong type, an unreadable document, an unsafe archive entry or a failed write is refused with a client-error and nothing is stored. A delete is refused while a run that uses the upload is not finished.

interfaces.name: client-error

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0

id.meaning: Immutable record identity

category.meaning: Stable reason family that a client may branch on: one of `auth`, `validation`, `not_found`, `conflict`, `unavailable`, `internal`. It is not user text.

message.meaning: Actionable explanation for the user. Display only. Never holds credentials or hidden fixtures.

request_id.meaning: Request this error answers, when known. Null otherwise.

run_id.meaning: Run this error concerns, when known. Null otherwise.

evidence_refs.meaning: Records the caller is authorized to see that explain the error. Empty when there are none.

correction.meaning: Action the user may take. A client never retries implicitly because of it.

interfaces.failure: Never include credentials/hidden fixtures or suggest implicit work retry.

interfaces.name: rsi-target-profile

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly `1.0.0`.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this target profile.

parent_ref.meaning: The one body file of the parent declaration that RSI may improve. Its digest is in `identity.body`.

frozen_contract_ref.meaning: Interface contract the child must keep unchanged. No candidate result may change it.

required_test_refs.meaning: Mandatory parent tests. The child must pass all of them.

mutable_paths.meaning: The only body paths the proposer may change. The target owner sets them inside what the CC author allowed in `may_change`, never the RSI operator or the proposer. A touched path outside this list is a security violation.

protected_refs.meaning: Files the proposer must not change and that the referee depends on. Never overlaps `mutable_paths`.

splits.meaning: Four distinct partition identities. The hidden ones are known only to the custodian and are never shown to the proposer.

scoring.meaning: Passed-tests-first scoring with a timing tie rule.

session_query_limit.meaning: Hidden-loop queries one session may spend, as a count. The baseline evaluation counts as one.

lifetime_query_limit.meaning: Hidden-loop queries over the lifetime of the registered loop set.

limits.meaning: Frozen bounds for every child run: `time_s` in seconds, `model_calls` as a count, `memory_mb` in MiB. Every value must be above zero here, stricter than the shared `Limits` type, because a child run with a zero bound cannot run. The target owner sets them. A candidate cannot change them.

configuration_ref.meaning: Frozen model, host and runtime settings, the same for parent and child.

interfaces.failure: No calibrated headroom, overlapping splits, a mutable path outside the parent `evolution.may_change`, or a mutable referee blocks the session. Never edit the profile in response to candidate results.

interfaces.name: rsi-attempt

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly `1.0.0`.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this attempt record.

sequence.meaning: Position of the attempt in the session, counted from 1 with no gap.

previous_ref.meaning: Previous attempt in the hash chain.

parent_ref.meaning: The same eligible parent on every attempt.

rationale.meaning: The proposer explanation. It is not proof and is never read as evidence.

visible_evidence_refs.meaning: Visible test results the proposer saw.

queries_used.meaning: Hidden-loop queries spent so far in the session, as a count. Copied from the custodian, never from the proposer.

violations.meaning: Violations the mutation check observed, as short descriptions. The mutation check writes them, never the proposer. A non-empty list ends the session at this attempt.

stop_reason.meaning: Why the session ended at this attempt, in plain words for the human reviewer. Written by the RSI controller. Null while the session continues. Must be set when `violations` is not empty. No check parses it: the outcome comes from the structured fields.

observation_refs.meaning: Protected model, time and call traces of the attempt, written by the RSI controller. For the referee, the evidence builder and people. The proposer never reads them.

time_s.meaning: Observed elapsed session time, in seconds. Null means unavailable, and null is never zero.

model_calls.meaning: Observed proposal model calls, as a count. Null means unavailable, and null is never zero.

unavailable_reasons.meaning: Why telemetry is missing. Missing telemetry is never reported as zero.

chain_root_ref.meaning: Protected genesis record. The first attempt never refers to itself.

interfaces.failure: A broken chain or lineage, an unauthorized mutation or a security violation halts the session and keeps the evidence. A clearance is needed before a new session.

interfaces.name: rsi-loop-feedback

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly `1.0.0`.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this loop feedback record.

passed.meaning: Aggregate hidden-loop passed count. A count only, with no case identity. The proposer reads this.

total.meaning: Hidden-loop case count, as a count. A count only, with no case identity.

queries_left.meaning: Hidden-loop queries still allowed in the session.

interfaces.failure: Counts only. No case IDs, content, timing, expected answers or final feedback enter the proposal context. A record with extra fields is refused.

interfaces.name: rsi-referee-evidence

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly `1.0.0`.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this referee evidence record.

pairs.meaning: Comparable repeated aggregate results of parent and child.

mandatory_parent_tests_passed.meaning: Whether the child passed every mandatory parent test.

integrity_passed.meaning: Whether custody, mutation and effect checks passed.

final_evaluations.meaning: Terminal evaluations the referee ran. A second one is a misuse of the final split.

configuration_ref.meaning: Exact comparable evaluation context of parent and child.

signature.meaning: The custodian's signature over the canonical JSON bytes of this record without `signature`. The referee writes it, running as `rsi_custodian`, only after its checks pass. `rsi_worker` cannot read the key (D46).

signer_key_id.meaning: ID of the signing key, not the key itself. A mismatch with the pinned ID blocks certification.

interfaces.failure: A wrong parent, fewer mandatory passes, a changed configuration, a reused final evaluation or tampering blocks certification.

interfaces.name: rsi-evidence-export

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly `1.0.0`.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this evidence export.

redactions.meaning: Names the kinds of content withheld (hidden cases, identities, answers, scoring detail), never the withheld content itself. Never empty.

interfaces.failure: A final export never feeds the loop. Withheld contents stay custodian-only. A hash does not grant read permission.

interfaces.name: library-admission

nodes.meaning: The fixed nodes. Same node shape as a plan proposal.

limits.meaning: Aggregate ceiling for the whole plan: `time_s` in seconds, `model_calls` as a count, `memory_mb` in MiB. The binder rejects limits above the plan policy `aggregate_limits` (`budget_ceilings`).

interfaces.failure: Reject before dispatch for a failed binder check. A template grants no authority.

interfaces.name: library-snapshot

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly 1.0.0.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this snapshot. The protected library sets it at capture. A new capture is a new record with a new ID.

captured_at.meaning: UTC time, to the second, when the protected library captured the snapshot. Later library changes never alter it.

entries.meaning: Eligible CC versions. Active library changes after capture never alter this list.

interfaces.failure: An entry with a null check pin is unusable. The binder rejects any node that names it.

interfaces.name: resource-inventory

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly 1.0.0.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this inventory. Host intake and capture set it.

resources.meaning: Resources supplied by the user or observed on the host. Host intake and capture write the list, never a CC. An empty list means no resource is available, so a node whose CC needs one fails `resource_feasibility`.

interfaces.failure: A missing resource makes every node that needs it infeasible. The binder rejects the plan.

interfaces.name: plan-policy

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly 1.0.0.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this policy. The protected configuration owner sets it.

max_nodes.meaning: Most nodes a plan may hold, as a count. It counts the nodes of the plan only, not the pre-plan Intention Compiler and Planner nodes.

allowed_effect_classes.meaning: Effect classes a node CC may have. M1 excludes `irreversible`.

allow_network.meaning: When false, no node may use a CC whose `network_mode` is not `none`.

required_stages.meaning: CCs that every plan holds, static or planned. Each named CC must have an eligible entry in the library snapshot the binder uses, or binding fails. Each runs in exactly one node. In M1: `research.search`, `research.screening` and `research.hypothesis`.

aggregate_limits.meaning: Ceiling for the whole plan, never changed by the Planner. `time_s` is in seconds and `memory_mb` in MiB. `model_calls` is a count. Time and calls add across nodes. Memory is the largest node value because M1 runs nodes one at a time.

max_attempts_per_node.meaning: Ceiling for `max_attempts` of any node, as a count of attempts. The M1 value is 1.

interfaces.failure: A plan outside the policy is rejected. The Planner cannot change the policy.

interfaces.name: run-plan

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly 1.0.0.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this frozen plan. The binder sets it at freeze.

plan_source.meaning: `static` when built from a static template. `planned` when built from a Planner proposal. Both use this same type.

library_snapshot_ref.meaning: Snapshot every CC pin was resolved against.

source_ref.meaning: The unmodified source the binder started from: for `static`, the template named by the operator config `cc.static_template_ref`; for `planned`, the accepted plan proposal.

acceptance_ref.meaning: Committed acceptance of the bound plan, from the plan gate. Dispatch cannot start without it.

nodes.meaning: Bound nodes with resolved accepted refs and copied check pins.

coverage.meaning: The coverage map after the binder expanded every selector of a static template against the accepted Brief (Selectors). It is the exact inverse of the node tags.

topological_order.meaning: Dispatch order computed by the binder with Kahn's algorithm. M1 runs nodes one at a time in this order.

limits.meaning: Aggregate ceiling for the whole plan. Constraint: same rule as a plan proposal.

frozen.meaning: Marks the plan immutable. After freeze there is no replan, substitution or pin change.

interfaces.failure: A missing acceptance record, an unresolved accepted ref or a missing pin blocks dispatch. Nothing in a frozen run plan may change.

interfaces.name: dispatch-record

schema_version.meaning: Format version 2.0.0. Reject any other value. Constraint: exactly 2.0.0.

id.meaning: Immutable ID of this record. The scheduler sets it.

run_id.meaning: Run this record belongs to. The host assigns it at intake. Every run-state record carries it.

attempt_id.meaning: Identity of this node attempt, for example `evaluation-a1`. The node contract, check plans and gate decisions of the attempt carry it.

phase.meaning: `pre_plan`: the Intention Compiler node or the Planner node, which run before a run plan exists. `planned`: a node of the frozen run plan.

cc.meaning: CC version that ran. The Intention Compiler node has two work CCs, pinned in its node contract.

node_contract_ref.meaning: Contract the attempt ran under. See From run plan node to execution contracts.

check_pins.meaning: Check bundle and profile that applied.

check_plan_ref.meaning: Bound check plan built for this attempt.

attempt.meaning: Attempt number. A new attempt is a new record.

started_at.meaning: Dispatch start time, set by the scheduler. UTC, to the second.

ended_at.meaning: End time of the attempt, set by the scheduler. UTC, to the second. Null means the attempt was interrupted and has no end.

outcome.meaning: How the attempt ended. `accepted`: the gate accepted the outputs. `rejected`: a blocking check or criterion failed, so the node halted and its candidate and evidence are kept. `halted`: protected stop. `failed`: execution or infrastructure error. `budget_exhausted`: a limit was hit. `interrupted`: the process ended before a decision.

output_gate_decision_refs.meaning: The per-output subnode-scope decisions that the node-scope decision aggregates, one for each output reviewed.

output_refs.meaning: Accepted outputs. Rejected output stays in evidence, not here.

elapsed_s.meaning: Observed wall time of the attempt in seconds, set by the scheduler. Null means not observed, never zero.

model_calls_used.meaning: Count of model calls the work subnode made through the model bridge during the attempt, set by the scheduler from bridge records. Verifier calls are counted on their own verifier subnode. M1 makes no routing selection call (`bounded_llm_ablation` is not built). Null means unobserved, never zero.

interfaces.failure: A record that names a node, pin or input not in the run plan is rejected and the dispatch is blocked. Records are append-only.

interfaces.name: search-scope
interfaces.producer: Protected binder (from run configuration, resource inventory and Planner topic hints)

schema_version.meaning: Format version 1.0.0. Format version

id.meaning: Record identity

brief_ref.meaning: The Brief this scope serves. Set by the protected binder, never by Search.

connectors.meaning: The retrieval sources Search may use. Anything not listed is forbidden. Set by the protected binder. Search may not add a connector.

max_queries.meaning: Most queries Search may write and run. A count. A hard bound set by the binder. Search may use fewer.

max_hits_per_query.meaning: Most distinct sources one external connector may contribute per query. A count. A hard bound set by the binder (`hit_limit`).

local_document_refs.meaning: The user's local documents Search may read. Refs set by the binder. Empty when `local_documents` is not a connector.

topic_hints.meaning: Optional topic phrases from the Planner. Search may use them when it writes queries. It may ignore them. They never replace the Brief and are not queries. Empty when `plan_source` is `static`.

interfaces.failure: A scope that fails its structure check blocks the Search dispatch. Search writes its own queries inside these bounds.

interfaces.name: candidate-set

schema_version.meaning: Format version 2.0.0. Format version

id.meaning: Record identity

scope_ref.meaning: The scope whose bounds Search ran under. Copied from the `search_scope` input (`scope_binding`).

queries.meaning: The queries Search itself wrote and ran, in run order. Written by Search. Plain query text, not taken from the scope. Every citation `query` is one of them.

connector_outcomes.meaning: What happened to each permitted connector, including failures. Search records one row per scope connector. It records `unavailable` and never fills a gap with invented sources.

citations.meaning: Exact excerpts captured from sources. Written by Search from captured bytes. The host checks each excerpt against the stored source. The verifier does not.
